chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever catches a thief and pardons him, that is for him; but if it is referred to the Imam, he will cut (his hand). If the one from whom it was stolen says, 'I forgive/pardon him,' the Imam will not leave him until he cuts (his hand) when it is referred to him.
And the pardon/forgiveness is only before it is referred to the Imam.
And those who guard the limits of Allah
So when it reaches the Imam, no one has the right to leave it (unexecuted).
ai.seo_question: Can the victim pardon a thief and prevent the Imam from cutting his hand?
ai.summary: This hadith from al--Istibsar delineates the distinction between private forgiveness (afw) and public justice (hudud) in Shia jurisprudence, asserting that the victim's pardon is valid only before the case reaches the Imam. Once referred, the Imam is bound by the divine command to 'guard the limits of Allah,' making the punishment obligatory rather than discretionary. This reflects the principle that hudud are rights of God, ensuring legal consistency even if the aggrieved party waives their personal claim.
